args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest production deploy) was failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18%. Rolled back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After rollback: all regions on v2.3.0, service is healthy, error rate is 0.2%. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging before v2.3.1 went to production. Follow-up: find the root cause in v2.3.1 and find out why it was promoted despite failing in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged the on-call engineer.

1. **Before the rollback:** All three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) were running v2.3.1. The service was failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
2. **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it. Since it has been healthy in production before, it didn't need change-manager approval.
3. **After the rollback:** All regions now run v2.3.0, health checks pass and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
4. **Incident:** There were no existing incidents for this. INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback and the current status.

I also noted in the incident that the test version of this release (v2.3.1-rc) failed health checks in staging before v2.3.1 was released to production. The follow-ups are to find the root cause in v2.3.1 and why it was released despite failing in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
